title: Choose the visual world — familiar hand
question: Real visual previews only — your final app build remains code-first. Choose the design that feels easiest to live with.

options.label: The Guided Reset
options.thesis: The app always shows one clear diagnosis, one next action, and one milestone instead of making you interpret a dashboard.
options.viewport: A calm summary names the current stage, explains why, and leads directly into a short Today / This Week / Next Milestone action list.
options.risk: The strong guidance leaves less room for users who prefer exploring all their numbers at once.

options.label: The Cashflow Calendar
options.thesis: Paydays, bills, and protected money live on one timeline so the user can see what must happen before the next check arrives.
options.viewport: The next fourteen days form the center of the dashboard, with each incoming paycheck and required bill placed in order above a safe-to-spend strip.
options.risk: Users focused on long-term debt payoff may find the date-first view less useful after they become stable.

options.label: The Spending Guardrails
options.thesis: Protected money and available money stay visibly separate, turning every spending category into a simple yes-or-not-yet decision.
options.viewport: A protected-money band sits above weekly grocery, fuel, restaurant, and date limits, with current spending directly compared to each limit.
options.risk: Category control is immediately useful but can feel budget-centric unless the recovery roadmap remains equally visible.

canonCard.label: Polished finance dashboard
canonCard.thesis: A familiar overview inspired by the clarity standards of YNAB, Monarch, and Copilot, without copying any one product.
canonCard.viewport: Account balances and summary cards lead, followed by spending charts, budget progress, upcoming bills, and recent activity.
canonCard.risk: Easy to recognize, but it places more burden on the user to interpret what the numbers mean and what to do next.
